entry.name: ADL-21
entry.title: Dataset of Tactile Signatures of the Human Right Hand in Twenty-One Activities of Daily Living Using a High Spatial Resolution Pressure Sensor
entry.summary: Tekscan Grip 4256E pressure sensor (361 sensels) sewn on a glove on the right hand of 22 subjects, each performing 21 activities of daily living once.
entry.hand: human right hand wearing a Tekscan Grip 4256E sensor sewn on a cotton glove, covered by polyethylene and latex gloves

sensor.note: One sample = 725 values in kPa (the 29x25 manufacturer matrix flattened; 361 active sensels in 18 regions on the volar hand, 364 inactive cells stored as -1). Sensel pitch 4 mm, 16 mm2 per sensel.

scale.text: ~1.8 h, 462 trials (21 ADL x 22 subjects, one each), 18 hand-held objects, 6 lab setups

entry.access: Open download from Zenodo: one 49.5 MB MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5) file, dataset.mat.
caveats: Tactile only: no video, no hand pose, no object pose.
Right hand only; the left hand also took part in tasks 7, 8, 11 and 15 but was not measured.
Each subject performed each task once, in one session.
presRaw keeps the full 29x25 manufacturer matrix: 364 of 725 columns are inactive cells filled with -1.
Grip force (GF) and per-region contribution (CGF) are released only on the 101-step normalized, cross-subject time-warped timeline, not per raw frame.
presRaw contains values above the 517 kPa sensor map (max 1630 kPa); the paper discarded saturated sensels in its analysis, but the release does not flag them.
subjectSex labels are not uniform: 'Woman', 'Man' and once 'Male'.

other: total grip force (N) and per-region contribution to grip force (18 regions)

unconfirmed: frames = 324,747: sum of presRaw row counts over the 462 trials in dataset.mat.
hours = 1.80: 324,747 rows / 50 Hz (paper sampling rate) = 6,494.9 s; mean 14.06 s per trial, matching the paper's 'close to 14 s'.
episodes = 462: dataset is a 21x22 struct array (task x subject), all 462 presRaw arrays non-empty; the paper says each subject performed each task once.

objects = 18 counts the items in the paper's Figure 2 (a-p, with (g) = spoon, knife, fork); Table 1 also lists fixtures and parts (door handle, water tap, drawer handle, bottle cup, tube cap, phone and keyboard keys) that are not counted.
scenes = 6 setups arranged in one laboratory (paper Figure 1), so scene_types = lab.
principle 'resistive' is the paper's wording ('thin resistive pressure sensor'); type 'piezoresistive' is the closest catalog class.
Value checks on dataset.mat: 0.008% of active pressure samples exceed 517 kPa, in 246 of 462 trials; 34 of the 361 active sensels never read above 0 in any trial.
GF equals 0.016 N/kPa x the sum of presInterpSync over active sensels (16 mm2 per sensel), checked on three trials to 1e-13.

channels.name: dataset(t,s).presRaw
channels.frame: Tekscan 4256E manufacturer matrix 29 rows x 25 cols, volar side of the right hand; column -> (row, col) via colSensel, see sensor.png
channels.note: Raw pressure per sensel over the trial. 361 active sensels; 364 inactive cells or gaps are -1 in every row. float64. Values 0..1629.6 kPa observed (sensor map 0-517 kPa).

channels.name: dataset(t,s).presInterpSync
channels.note: Pressure interpolated to normalized time steps of 0.01 (101 samples per trial) and time-warped to the task's reference subject; not a fixed sampling rate.

channels.name: dataset(t,s).GF
channels.note: Scalar total grip force: sum of sensel forces (pressure x 16 mm2) on the normalized, synchronized timeline. Equals 0.016 x sum(presInterpSync over active sensels).

channels.name: dataset(t,s).CGF
channels.frame: 18 anatomical sensing regions (paper Table 3: 1-2 thumb distal/proximal, 3-14 index..little distal/intermediate/proximal, 15 distal palm 2nd metacarpal, 16 distal palm 3rd-5th metacarpal, 17 thenar, 18 hypothenar)
channels.note: Per-region fraction of grip force on the normalized timeline; rows sum to 1.

channels.name: dataset(t,s).task
channels.note: Task description, same text as tasks{t}.

channels.name: dataset(t,s).subjectSex
channels.note: 'Woman' (12 subjects) / 'Man' (9) / 'Male' (1, subject 4); constant per subject across tasks.

channels.name: dataset(t,s).refSubj
channels.note: Reference subject used for time synchronization of this task.

channels.name: dataset(t,s).indexSync
channels.note: [i1ref, i2ref, i1, i2] rows used for time warping.

channels.name: tasks
channels.note: Global: task descriptions in task-index order.

channels.name: colSensel
channels.note: Global: presRaw column -> matrix (row, col). In sensor.png the thumb regions are at matrix cols 1-4 (drawn at the right), fingers at the top rows 1-12.

sample.fetch_estimate: 0 MB more: the full release (dataset.mat, 49,542,130 B) is already in ~/data/ext/adl21/. No video or other media to re-host (touch only); converted episode JSON is about 0.3-0.9 MB each (361 sensels x 532-1796 frames as Uint8 + base64, plus the 101-step GF/CGF series), ~4 MB for all 8.
sample.rules_applied: 21 tasks > 6, so 8 tasks were taken: at least one from each of the 6 setups (1: key/lock; 2: pen, keyboard; 3: bottle+pour, knife; 4: drawer+comb; 5: window cloth; 6: iron), covering precision pinch, tripod writing, tapping, twisting/pouring, cutting, pulling+combing, wiping and push-sliding, with 8 different objects. One episode per task, 8 different subjects (4 Man incl. subject 4 'Male', 4 Woman). All trials are right-hand only (one instrumented glove), so no two-handed episode exists. Duration rule 10-60 s: no trial exceeds 60 s (max 51.2 s) so every window is null; 147 of 462 trials are under 10 s, which excludes task 21 (briefcase lift, all 22 trials 3.9-8.0 s) and leaves tasks 3 and 13 with one usable trial and tasks 6/7/17/19 with 2-3. Within each task the passing trial closest to the task's median duration with a long continuous contact was preferred, while keeping subjects distinct. Contact check on presRaw (active sensels only): frames with total force (0.016 N/kPa x sum over 361 sensels) > 5 N and at least 3 sensels > 10 kPa; every pick has a continuous contact run of 3.3-8.2 s, and rest at the start is 0.0-0.5 kPa mean. Channel check on each pick: presRaw (N,725) with exactly 361 active columns, the 364 inactive columns -1 in every row, no NaN, no negative values, no sensel stuck at a constant non-zero value; presInterpSync (101,725) no NaN; GF (101,) equals 0.016 x sum of active presInterpSync to < 2e-14; CGF (101,18) rows sum to 1 where GF > 0 and are all zero where GF = 0 (this is the case for 134 of 462 trials, e.g. t07 s09, and is not corruption); iColRegion has 18 regions totalling 361 sensels. Release-wide, 34 of the 361 active sensels are 0 in every one of the 462 trials (16 in region 16 distal palm 3rd-5th metacarpal, 8/5/2 in the little finger regions 12-14, 3 in region 5 index proximal); dead or never loaded cannot be told apart. 246 of 462 trials have raw peaks above the 517 kPa sensor map (picks: 0-0.019% of samples above it). GF/CGF/presInterpSync exist only on the 101-step normalized, time-warped timeline and cannot be aligned to presRaw's 50 Hz clock sample by sample.
